Good afternoon. I taught geography for thirty-eight years and now, in my retirement, I help on Tuesdays at our town library, where we have been asked to prepare a plan of the rooms for the new volunteers. I must admit I had never used a program of this kind until my grandson showed me, and I find it rather clever, though he is not here today to help. You will see that the globe sits in the reading room, and that is quite correct, as it has been there since before my time. However, the large stacks you have drawn at the upper right should be named the Local History Collection, since the plain word stacks means nothing to a newcomer. I wonder whether you might also put a little table beside the globe, a square would do nicely. The entrance is correct where it stands. There ought to be a line showing how a visitor walks from the entrance to the reading room, and from there on to the collection, and I should like that line to be in a dark colour so that it may be seen from a distance. We used to keep the atlases on a separate stand, but they went to the school in 2011 and that need not concern you. If it is not too much trouble, a heading across the top would finish it off: Our Library, A Plan for Volunteers. Thank you most kindly for your patience with an old teacher.
